proof_summary: Writing \(X=2^{2^{33}}\), the inequality \(\varphi(m)<m\) gives the lower bound \(m\ge X+1=F_{33}\), attained when \(F_{33}\) is prime. If \(F_{33}\) is composite, assuming \(m<2X\) forces \(\varphi(m)=X\); after writing \(m=2^k r\) with \(r\) odd, \(k\ge2\) contradicts this bound using \(\varphi(r)<r\), while \(k\le1\) would make \(r\) squarefree with all prime factors among the Fermat primes \(F_i\) for \(i<33\), so \(r\le\prod_{i<33}F_i=F_{33}-2<X<r\); hence the attainable candidate \(2X\) is minimal.
